chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Khazzaz, from Harun ibn Kharrajah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said to me: 'O Harun ibn Kharrajah, what is the distance between you and the Masjid of Kufa? Is it a mile?' I said, 'No.' He said: 'So you pray all the prayers in it?' I said, 'No.' So he said: 'If I were in its vicinity, I would hope that not a single prayer would be missed by me in it. And do you know the merit of that place?'

There is no righteous servant nor a Prophet except that he has prayed in the Masjid of Kufa. To the extent that when Allah ascended His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Do you know where you are at this moment, O Messenger of Allah? You are facing the Masjid of Kufa.'
He said: 'Ask my Lord for permission for me so that I may go to it and pray two Rak'at in it.' So he asked Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for permission, and He granted it to him.
And its right side is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and its middle is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and its rear is a garden from the gardens of Paradise.
And the obligatory prayer in it equals a thousand prayers, and the optional prayer in it equals five hundred prayers, and sitting in it without recitation or remembrance is worship.
And if people knew what is in it, they would go to it, even if they had to crawl.
Sahl said: 'And it was reported to me by someone other than Amr that the prayer in it equals one Hajj, and the optional prayer in it equals one Umrah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual merit and reward of praying in the Masjid of Kufa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the unique spiritual status of the Masjid of Kufa, linking it to the Prophet's Mi'raj and affirming that every righteous servant and Prophet has prayed there. It details the specific rewards for prayers performed in its different sections, noting that obligatory prayers equal a thousand and optional prayers equal five hundred, while mere sitting is considered worship. The narration also includes a variant report equating the reward of an obligatory prayer to a Hajj and an optional prayer to an Umrah, highlighting its significance as a beloved place of worship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Al-Hassan, and Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Amro Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Al-Khazzaz, from Haroun Bin Kharjat who said, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Haroun Bin Kharjat!

How much (distance) is there between you and Masjid Al-Kufa, would it happen to be a mile?’ I said, ‘No’. Heasws said: ‘So you pray all of the Salāts in it?’ I said, ‘No’. So heasws said: ‘But, if Iasws was in its vicinity, Iasws would have wished that not a Salāt would have been missed out by measws in it, and do you know what is the merit of that place?

There is none from a righteous servant, nor a Prophetas except that he has prayed Salāt in Masjid of Kufa, to the extent that Rasool-Allahsaww, when Allahsaww ascended himsaww, Jibraeelas said to himsaww: ‘Do yousaww know where yousaww are at the moment, O Rasool-Allahsaww? Yousaww are facing Masjid of Kufa’.

He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So ask my<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> to Permit for me<sup>saww</sup>, until I<sup>saww</sup> go over to it, and prayed two Rak’at therein’. 
So he<sup>as</sup> sought Permission of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and He<sup>azwj</sup> Permitted for him<sup>saww</sup>.

And one the right of it is a garden from the Gardens of the Paradise, and in the middle of it is a garden from the Gardens of the Paradise, and at the back of it is a garden from the Gardens of the Paradise; and an Obligatory Salāt performed therein equates to a thousand Salāts, and the optional (Salāt) performed therein equates to five hundred Salāts; and the sitting in it without a recitation or a mention is worship; and had the people known what is therein, they would go to it, even if they had to crawl’.
Sahl (the narrator) said, ‘And it was reported to me from someone other than Amro that the (Obligatory) Salāt in it equates to one Hajj, and that the optional (Salāt) in it equates to an Umra’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn al-Hassan and Ali ibn Muhammad have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Khazzaz from Harun ibn Kharijah who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked me, ‘O Harun ibn Kharijah, how far away do you live from the Masjid of Kufah?

Is it one mile?’ I replied, ‘No, it is less than a mile.’ He then asked, ‘Do you perform all Salah (prayers) there?’ I replied, ‘No, I do not perform all Salah (prayers) there.’ He then said, ‘If I were nearby I hope I would not miss performing any Salah (prayer) therein. Do you know what is the excellence of Salah (prayer) performed therein?

There is no believer of good deeds or prophet who has not performed Salah (prayer) in the Masjid of Kufah. Even when the Messenger of Allah was on his night journey, Jibril asked him, “Do you know where your are, O Messenger of Allah? At this hour you are across the Masjid of Kufah.”
He said, “Ask my Lord for permission so I can go there and perform two Rak‘at Salah (prayer) therein.” He asked Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, for permission, which was granted.

On the right side of this Masjid, there is a garden of the gardens of paradise, in the middle of it, there is a garden of the gardens of paradise and behind it, there is a garden of the gardens of paradise.

Performing one obligatory Salah (prayer) in it is equal to one thousand Salah (prayer). One optional Salah (prayer) in it is equal to five hundred Salah (prayer). Sitting in it without performing any Salah (prayer) or speaking of Allah is worshipping.
Had people known its excellence they would go to it even crawling.’
Sahl has said that narrators other than ‘Amr have said that performing obligatory Salah (prayer) in it is equal to performing Hajj and performing optional Salah (prayer) is equal to ‘Umrah.”
